|archive-date=9 June 2018}}</ref> Business executives [[Jack Ma]] and [[JP Morgan Chase]] CEO [[Jamie Dimon]] have called it in 2017–2018 a "bubble"<ref name="Yang Ma">{{cite news |last1=Yang |first1=Yingzhi |date=18 May 2018 |title=There's a bitcoin bubble, says Alibaba executive chairman Jack Ma |publisher=South China Morning Post |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/enterprises/article/2146648/theres-bitcoin-bubble-says-alibaba-executive-chairman-jack-ma |url-status=live |access-date=10 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180610214759/http://www.scmp.com/tech/enterprises/article/2146648/theres-bitcoin-bubble-says-alibaba-executive-chairman-jack-ma |archive-date=10 June 2018}}</ref> and a "fraud",<ref name="Buffet and Dimon">{{cite news |last1=Cheng |first1=Evelyn |date=7 June 2018 |title=Warren Buffett and Jamie Dimon on bitcoin: Beware |publisher=CNBC |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/06/07/warren-buffett-and-jamie-dimon-on-bitcoin-beware.html |url-status=live |access-date=7 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180609122312/https://www.cnbc.com/2018/06/07/warren-buffett-and-jamie-dimon-on-bitcoin-beware.html |archive-date=9 June 2018}}</ref> respectively, although Jamie Dimon later said in 2018 that he regretted stating bitcoin was a fraud.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kim |first=Tae |date=9 January 2018 |title=Jamie Dimon says he regrets calling bitcoin a fraud and believes in the technology behind it |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/09/jamie-dimon-says-he-regrets-calling-bitcoin-a-fraud.html |access-date=31 December 2020 |website=CNBC |language=en |archive-date=13 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113085325/https://www.cnbc.com/2018/01/09/jamie-dimon-says-he-regrets-calling-bitcoin-a-fraud.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[BlackRock]] CEO [[Laurence D. Fink]] in 2017 called bitcoin an "index of [[money laundering]]".<ref>{{cite web |last=Imbert |first=Fred |date=13 October 2017 |title=BlackRock CEO Larry Fink calls bitcoin an 'index of money laundering' |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/10/13/blackrock-ceo-larry-fink-calls-bitcoin-an-index-of-money-laundering.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030202248/https://www.cnbc.com/2017/10/13/blackrock-ceo-larry-fink-calls-bitcoin-an-index-of-money-laundering.html |archive-date=30 October 2017 |access-date=19 November 2017 |website=[[CNBC]]}}</ref>

In June 2022, business magnate [[Bill Gates]] said that cryptocurrencies are "100% based on [[greater fool theory]]".<ref>{{cite web |last=Browne |first=Ryan |date=15 June 2022 |title=Bill Gates says crypto and NFTs are '100% based on greater fool theory' |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2022/06/15/bill-gates-says-crypto-and-nfts-are-based-on-greater-fool-theory.html |access-date=15 June 2022 |website=[[CNBC]] |archive-date=15 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615081326/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/06/15/bill-gates-says-crypto-and-nfts-are-based-on-greater-fool-theory.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Legal scholars criticize the lack of regulation, which hinders conflict resolution when crypto assets are at the center of a legal dispute, for example a divorce or an inheritance. In Switzerland, jurists generally deny that cryptocurrencies are objects that fall under [[property law]], as cryptocurrencies do not belong to any class of legally defined objects (''Typenzwang'', the legal [[Numerus clausus (law)|numerus clausus]]). Therefore, it is debated whether anybody could even be sued for [[embezzlement]] of cryptocurrency if they had access to someone's wallet. However, in the [[law of obligations]] and [[Contract|contract law]], any kind of object would be legally valid, but the object would have to be tied to an identified [[counterparty]]. However, inasmuch the more popular cryptocurrencies can be freely and quickly exchanged into legal tender, they are financial assets and have to be taxed and accounted for as such.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=Aktuelles zum Recht der Kryptowährungen |journal=Aktuelle Juristische Praxis / Pratique Juridique Actuelle |url=https://www.alexandria.unisg.ch/259362/1/MUELLER_ONG_AJP_02_2020_198-212.pdf |last1=Müller |first1=Lukas |issue=2 |last2=Ong |first2=Malik |date=17 February 2020 |language=de |trans-title=Current state of the law of crypto currencies |access-date=17 February 2023 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210174829/https://www.alexandria.unisg.ch/259362/1/MUELLER_ONG_AJP_02_2020_198-212.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Baer |first1=Katherine |last2=De Mooij |first2=Ruud |last3=Hebous |first3=Shafik |last4=Keen |first4=Michael |title=Taxing cryptocurrencies |journal=[[Oxford Review of Economic Policy]] |date=2023 |volume=39 |issue=3 |pages=478–497 |doi=10.1093/oxrep/grad035 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Losses associated with cryptocurrency investments have been linked to suicides.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emem |first=Mark |date=12 June 2019 |title=Chinese Bitcoin Trader Commits Suicide after Losing 2,000 BTC on 100x Leverage Bet |url=https://www.ccn.com/bitcoin-margin-100x-leverage-trader-suicide/ |access-date=31 October 2025 |website=CCN.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Holly |last2=Sharman |first2=Laura |date=17 February 2022 |title=Bitcoin trader, 23, takes own life after break-up and losing all his money |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/heartbroken-man-took-life-after-26260173 |access-date=2 May 2022 |website=Mirror |language=en |archive-date=2 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220502035724/https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/heartbroken-man-took-life-after-26260173 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2018, an increase in crypto-related suicides was noticed after the cryptocurrency market crashed in August.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} The situation was particularly critical in Korea as crypto traders were on "suicide watch".{{citation needed|date=October 2025}} The May 2022 collapse of the Luna currency operated by [[Terra (blockchain)|Terra]] also led to reports of suicidal investors in crypto-related subreddits.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sarlin |first1=Jon |title=Stablecoins were supposed to be 'stable.' Then the crash came |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/05/17/investing/luna-terra-losses-crypto-traders/index.html |access-date=30 May 2022 |publisher=CNN |date=17 May 2022 |archive-date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529222016/https://www.cnn.com/2022/05/17/investing/luna-terra-losses-crypto-traders/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
